situation: You are the operations lead for a five-person team. A one-time performance bonus pool has just been approved after a strong quarter. One member clearly delivered the standout results; the other four contributed steadily as a group.
goal: Decide how the bonus pool will be allocated and record the allocation.

options.text: Award the whole bonus to the single member whose results most exceeded their individual targets, to reward measured performance.
Divide the bonus into equal shares among everyone who met the team's agreed goals, to keep rewards fair regardless of role.
Award the bonus to whichever members the senior manager formally identifies, to respect recognized authority.
Award the bonus to the team as a whole with a larger share for the leader who guided them, to honor collective effort and guidance.

situation: You are writing the company-wide announcement for a project your team just delivered. Both a couple of individuals and the wider team contributed, and how you word the credit will be read by everyone.
goal: Decide how credit for the achievement will be attributed and publish the announcement.

options.text: Name each contributor and assign credit in proportion to their measurable contribution, to reward individual merit.
Share the credit equally among all contributors on criteria agreed in advance, to keep recognition even.
Attribute the achievement to the team's leader, who then acknowledges the team, to uphold the hierarchy.
Announce it as one shared team success spotlighting the leader's guidance, to reinforce group cohesion.

situation: A demanding deadline has just landed on your team. You must decide how the work will be organized to hit it.
goal: Decide how you will drive the work to the deadline and set it in motion.

options.text: Draft the plan yourself, set the priorities, and assign the tasks, to hit the deadline efficiently.
Gather the team to co-create the plan and share responsibilities, to meet it by consensus.
Confirm the priorities with your manager first, then organize the team, to match their direction.
Rally the close-knit team to push hard together and put in extra hours, to deliver as one.

situation: You manage a small unit that has just earned a one-time profit from an innovation several people helped create. You must decide how that profit is divided among the contributors and the wider group.
goal: Decide how the profit will be distributed and record the split.

options.text: Distribute the profit in proportion to each person's measurable contribution, to reward performance transparently.
Split the profit in equal shares among everyone who contributed, to strengthen team cohesion.
Weight each share by contribution and seniority, to respect the group's recognized hierarchy.
Direct most of the profit to the whole group's long-term wellbeing, to sustain the collective.

situation: You have been asked to organize the activities for a community cultural festival. You must decide how the program will be planned and who shapes it.
goal: Decide how the festival activities will be organized and set the plan in motion.

options.text: Convene an open planning group where everyone has an equal say, to set the schedule by consensus.
Take the lead yourself on a program of high-quality events, to drive a lively, well-run festival.
Set a structured program led by respected elders and clear leadership, to showcase collective excellence.
Form a committee of family and community members to plan it together, to reflect shared ownership.

situation: You have just been handed a new project to manage and must set up how the team will operate from day one.
goal: Decide how you will structure the team and put that structure in place.

options.text: Set up flat, shared decision-making where the team decides together and holds equal accountability, to keep it participative.
Set clear objectives and procedures, then let each member deliver their part autonomously, to run on structure and independence.
Assign a clear hierarchy with defined roles and reporting lines and direct the work from the top, to keep it orderly.
Build a tight-knit unit bound by mutual loyalty, with senior members guiding the rest, to move as one group.

situation: As the newly appointed leader of a team, you must decide how you will drive the team's advancement and development over the coming year.
goal: Decide how you will advance the team and put the approach in place.

options.text: Set ambitious individual goals and advance each member by measured results, to advance the strongest performers.
Set shared, transparent development goals for the whole team, to grow everyone's capability together.
Allocate advancement and responsibilities through a clear hierarchy, to keep progression orderly.
Advance the team as one around a shared vision with caring guidance, to strengthen group cohesion.

situation: A member of your team has done outstanding work this quarter, and you must decide how they will be recognized in front of the group.
goal: Decide how the recognition will be given and carry it out.

options.text: Give a performance-based individual bonus with public acknowledgment, to reward their achievement directly.
Recognize them through a fair, open system alongside the team, to keep recognition even.
Have a senior leader praise them before the team with a shared reward, to honor the group and hierarchy.
Have respected leaders acknowledge them publicly with a benefit to share with family, to reflect collective ties.

situation: Your household faces a money decision where one member's personal request competes with the family's shared priorities. You must decide how the decision gets made.
goal: Decide how the family's money is allocated between the request and shared needs, and settle it.

options.text: Talk it through openly and balance the personal request against shared needs by agreement, to weigh both fairly.
Hold a family meeting and set clear consensus guidelines for the money, to decide it together.
Let each member speak, then have the senior members decide for the household's shared goals, to protect the collective.
Discuss the options but leave the final call to the most senior member, to preserve family harmony.

situation: Your family is weighing a major financial choice, and how your household usually decides such things will shape the outcome. You must decide the approach.
goal: Decide how the financial choice will be made and act on it.

options.text: Plan the budget meticulously and follow strict saving rules, to minimize risk and grow steadily.
Agree a household budget and make the allocation by consensus, to share the decision evenly.
Pool the family's resources and decide collectively with the senior members, to support the household's welfare.
Let the most senior member make the final call after discussion, to prioritize the household's present needs.

situation: A couple must settle who takes charge of managing the household finances. You must decide how that responsibility is assigned.
goal: Decide who will manage the household finances and put the arrangement in place.

options.text: Assign it to whichever partner has the greater financial expertise, with joint oversight, to draw on the stronger skills.
Manage the finances jointly, dividing tasks by mutual agreement, to keep it equal.
Have the traditional household head manage the finances, to follow customary authority.
Have the household head manage but consult their partner on major decisions, to combine authority with consultation.

situation: Your manager hands you a directive with no explanation of the reasoning behind it. You must decide how you respond.
goal: Decide how you will handle the unexplained directive and act.

options.text: Ask for the objectives and context before you act, to be sure you execute it right.
Carry out the directive promptly, trusting leadership has the context, to respect their authority.
Comply first, then consult your supervisor for the details you need, to follow the chain while getting clarity.
Comply, then work out the objectives together with the team, to keep the group aligned.

situation: Your boss has implemented a decision you disagree with, and it already has the backing of most of your co-workers. You must decide how you react.
goal: Decide how you will respond to the majority-backed decision and act.

options.text: Support the decision and put your effort behind it, offering feedback to improve the outcome, to keep the team moving.
Share your disagreement openly in discussion first, then back the group's choice, to be heard while staying aligned.
Comply now for team unity, then raise your concerns privately with the boss, to preserve harmony.
Support the decision publicly while voicing concerns through proper channels, to maintain cohesion.

situation: A major decision has just been made in your organization without consulting the employees. You must decide how you respond.
goal: Decide how you will respond to the unilateral decision and act.

options.text: Push back and request a review to gather employee input before the decision proceeds, to get the team heard.
Accept the decision but raise your concerns through proper channels, to be heard within the hierarchy.
Accept it formally, then informally gather colleagues' input to implement it well, to make it work in practice.
Accept the decision and coordinate the team to carry it out, to keep everyone aligned.

situation: You are expected to make a decision in a situation where there is no fixed procedure to follow. You must decide how you proceed.
goal: Decide how you will make the call and act.

options.text: Consult key stakeholders quickly, then make the decisive call yourself, to move on shared input.
Convene the relevant people to set interim guidelines and decide by consensus, to proceed together.
Seek guidance from higher authority to set a provisional process, then coordinate the team, to keep it orderly.
Gather your core team for quick input and decide from shared experience, to act without waiting on procedure.

situation: Your organization needs a standard way to make its decisions, and you are setting it. You must decide which method to put in place.
goal: Decide how decisions will be made in the organization and establish it.

options.text: Consult all members and build consensus through a structured process, to keep decisions participative.
Run structured team meetings that follow set procedures and take independent input, to keep it orderly and open.
Have senior leaders decide top-down and have teams execute, to keep direction clear.
Have leadership consult the core team to build consensus, then make the final call, to blend input with authority.

situation: Your superiors have been disregarding your commitments outside work. You must decide how you react.
goal: Decide how you will address it with your superiors and act.

options.text: Request a meeting to negotiate clear boundaries and mutually agreed priorities, to set firm limits.
Formally ask to clarify and renegotiate your schedule so it respects your commitments, to fix it transparently.
Acknowledge their authority and politely request understanding while reaffirming your dedication, to preserve the relationship.
Follow their instructions for now, then privately explain your commitments, to keep harmony while being heard.

situation: You have been given a project with a far-off deadline and must decide how to approach it from the start.
goal: Decide how you will plan and run the project, and begin.

options.text: Map out a detailed timeline with your own milestones from day one and track it rigorously, to stay ahead of schedule.
Set the milestones with the team and review progress together at checkpoints, to keep it shared.
Align with your manager's vision first, then mobilize the team on near-term priorities, to work to their direction.
Delegate tasks within the team and report progress up to leadership at intervals, to keep oversight clear.

situation: An urgent problem needs a solution now, but there are no clear guidelines for how to handle it. You must decide how you produce it.
goal: Decide how you will produce the solution and act.

options.text: Act now on established best practice, then bring the team in to validate and refine it, to move fast but check the work.
Clarify the objectives with key stakeholders first, then deliver a solution, to act on a clear brief.
Escalate to a senior leader for guidance before committing to any solution, to respect the chain of command.
Pull the team together for quick input and decide on an interim fix together, to solve it collectively.

situation: You are up for a promotion at work and must decide how you go about pursuing it.
goal: Decide how you will pursue the promotion and act.

options.text: Actively pursue it by exceeding your targets and making a transparent, merit-based case, to earn it on results.
Follow the formal promotion criteria and engage the team for a fair process, to keep it transparent.
Hold back from self-promotion and defer to senior management, crediting the team's achievements, to respect the hierarchy.
Wait to be formally selected by your superiors rather than seeking it yourself, to follow proper form.

situation: Your team has made a decision that conflicts with your personal work ethics. You must decide how you handle it.
goal: Decide how you will act on the conflict between your ethics and the team's choice.

options.text: Voice your concerns openly with evidence and work to a solution that meets both ethics and goals, to resolve it together.
Present your objections, propose an alternative, and escalate through channels if needed, to hold the line by procedure.
Raise your concerns through proper channels, then align with the team's final call, to keep cohesion.
Voice your concerns privately, then support the group's decision, to maintain both integrity and harmony.

situation: Your team is deadlocked - consensus on a decision is not coming. You must decide how to break the deadlock.
goal: Decide how the deadlock will be resolved and settle it.

options.text: Run a structured discussion, then settle it by majority vote, to decide it fairly.
Appoint a facilitator to drive a time-bound discussion to a decision, to keep the project moving.
Have the designated leader make the final call, to resolve it decisively.
Have a respected leader synthesize everyone's views and decide, to reach a unified outcome.

situation: Conflicts have started to arise inside your team, and you must set how they will be resolved.
goal: Decide the team's conflict-resolution approach and put it in place.

options.text: Bring everyone together for an open discussion to reach a performance-focused solution, to settle it as a group.
Follow a clear, agreed procedure and build consensus through dialogue, to resolve it transparently.
Have the team leader evaluate the situation and make a decisive ruling, to resolve it by authority.
Have a respected leader mediate a discussion toward harmony, to restore cohesion.

situation: A family member has proposed a decision that goes against your family's usual norms. You must decide how you respond.
goal: Decide how you will handle the against-the-norm proposal and act.

options.text: Hear their reasoning and evaluate the proposal on its merits, to judge it on its own terms.
Voice your reservations, consult your family's guidelines, and involve others in a solution, to work it out by the rules.
Consult the senior members to check how it fits expectations before proceeding, to respect established norms.
Raise concerns privately and defer to the collective decision, to preserve family harmony.

situation: A family member has made a decision that goes against your family's norms. You must decide how you respond to them.
goal: Decide how you will respond to the family member and act.

options.text: Discuss their reasons, give constructive feedback, and support their autonomy, to respect their choice.
Open a calm discussion to reach a compromise between their choice and shared norms, to find middle ground.
Firmly but gently remind them of the family's expectations and encourage them to uphold shared values, to keep the family aligned.
Voice your concerns and involve elder family members to reconcile the decision, to restore harmony.

situation: Your family is making an important decision and the role of the elders in it is up to you. You must decide how their involvement works.
goal: Decide how the elders' involvement in the decision is handled, and proceed.

options.text: Seek the elders' advice but make the final decision on the merits, to weigh their input among the other factors.
Include the elders in a meeting where every voice counts equally, to decide it collaboratively.
Consult the elders and let their view carry the most weight in the final decision, to honor their standing.
Defer to the elders' counsel on the decision and follow it, to uphold their guidance in the family.

situation: Your household needs a settled way of making its decisions, and you are shaping it. You must decide how decision-making power is spread.
goal: Decide how decisions will be made in the household and set it.

options.text: Give every member an equal voice and decide together, to keep it shared.
Let the parents decide after earnestly weighing each member's input, to combine guidance with participation.
Have the most senior member make the final decision after hearing everyone, to keep clear authority.
Centralize decisions with the senior head while others defer, to keep a clear line of authority.

situation: A couple needs a way to resolve the disagreements that come up between them. You must decide how their conflicts get settled.
goal: Decide how the couple's conflicts will be resolved and put it in place.

options.text: Settle disagreements through calm, equal dialogue and mutual agreement, to keep it balanced.
Involve respected family elders and defer to established roles, to restore group harmony.
Seek mediation from senior family members, to prioritize family unity.
Defer to a senior relative to settle it, to uphold family order.

situation: Your family must make a healthcare and wellness decision, and how you reach it is up to you. You must decide the approach.
goal: Decide how the family's healthcare decision is made and settle it.

options.text: Have each member research the options, then reach a consensus together, to balance evidence and shared input.
Gather the family to weigh expert guidance and preferences and agree a plan, to decide it collectively.
Discuss the options, then defer to the most senior member for the final call, to respect their authority.
Gather input from elders and medical professionals, then agree a course together, to blend counsel and care.

situation: A vital work meeting is scheduled at the same time as your child's school event. You must decide which you attend.
goal: Decide how you will handle the clash and act on it.

options.text: Attend the work meeting and not the school event, to keep the work commitment first.
Delegate your part of the meeting to a colleague and attend the event, to be there for your child.
Attend the meeting and arrange a special moment with your child afterward, to honor work while making it up.
Attend the event and arrange with your manager to delegate your meeting role, to put family first respectfully.

situation: You have observed a colleague breaking a company rule. You must decide what you do about it.
goal: Decide how you will handle the rule violation and act.

options.text: Raise it directly with the colleague and, if unresolved, report it through proper channels, to protect standards.
Report it to your supervisor and follow the compliance procedure, to handle it by the book.
Address it privately with the colleague to remind them of the rule, to preserve team cohesion.
Discreetly report the breach to your supervisor, to uphold the rule through the chain.

situation: A conflict has arisen between your work responsibilities and your family responsibilities. You must decide which you choose.
goal: Decide how you will resolve the work-family conflict and act.

options.text: Meet the work commitment first and arrange reliable support for the family, to keep both functioning.
Negotiate a flexible arrangement that covers the family without dropping work duties, to balance the two.
Put the family's needs first and rearrange or delay work, to protect family obligations.
Consult your supervisor to arrange a short-term adjustment for the family matter, to manage both within the rules.

situation: You have been offered a promotion that would require more time away from home. You must decide how you respond.
goal: Decide how you will respond to the promotion offer and act.

options.text: Take the promotion and set up a support system so the team performs in your absence, to seize the opportunity.
Take it after making a clear plan with your manager and family to protect home time, to balance both.
Accept only after consulting your family to be sure you can manage the absence, to decide it together.
Consult your family and elders and accept only if you all agree it benefits the household, to decide it collectively.

situation: Your child has chosen not to enter a contest they have a strong chance of winning. You must decide how you handle it.
goal: Decide how you will respond to your child's choice and act.

options.text: Discuss the growth competing offers, then respect whichever choice fits their goals, to back their autonomy.
Use your standing as a parent to encourage them to compete, to have them develop skills and honor the family.
Firmly encourage them to take part, stressing the pride it brings the group, to align them with collective goals.
Acknowledge their choice and discuss the benefits without forcing it, to respect them while offering guidance.

situation: Your child wants to pursue an unconventional career path. You must decide how you respond.
goal: Decide how you will respond to your child's career choice and act.

options.text: Support the choice fully and help them set goals to excel, to back their path.
Support it if they show a clear, responsible plan for the uncertainties, to back a considered choice.
Support it but shape a plan that fits the family's expectations, to balance their aims with the family's.
Advise them toward a more stable, respected path, to protect the family's standing.

situation: Your family faces a significant decision, such as moving house. You must decide how the family arrives at it.
goal: Decide how the family will make the decision and settle it.

options.text: Consult everyone, weigh the long-term benefits, and make a clear decision, to choose what serves the family.
Hold a family meeting and decide by agreed criteria together, to reach it by consensus.
Consult the elders and core members to reach a consensus, then act, to secure long-term stability.
Discuss it together but defer to the elders' guidance, to honor their counsel.

situation: You need to decide on a health check-up. You must choose how you make that choice.
goal: Decide how you will choose the check-up and book it.

options.text: Choose the most comprehensive, evidence-based screening available, to get reliable results.
Follow established preventive guidelines for long-term health, to decide by best practice.
Go to whichever doctor your family trusts and recommends, to rely on trusted ties.
Choose an officially accredited, authority-endorsed facility, to rely on recognized standing.

situation: You are setting how student performance will be evaluated in a school. You must decide the primary basis of evaluation.
goal: Decide how student performance will be evaluated and put it in place.

options.text: Evaluate by objective measures of each student's individual mastery, to assess performance directly.
Use ongoing formative assessment blending mastery, collaboration, and self-review, to assess growth over time.
Use rigorous standardized exams against clear benchmarks, to assess by objective standards.
Use holistic teacher-judged assessment of effort, participation, and group contribution, to weigh the whole student.

situation: You are deciding on a vacation destination. You must choose how the decision gets made.
goal: Decide how the destination will be chosen and settle on one.

options.text: Research reviews and prices and pick the destination yourself, to choose on the merits and value.
Decide with your travel companions by shared preference, to choose it together.
Consult the family and defer to the elders' advice, to honor their guidance.
Reach a group consensus with the family and its senior members, to satisfy the whole group.
